4) A thing can be in more than one “way” at once
Before we look, a tiny thing may not have one clear place or one clear push. It can be in a mix of possible ways. When we measure, we get one clear result.

5) Two far things can still act linked
Sometimes two tiny things are made together in a way that links their results. If you test one, you learn something about the other, even far away.

These rules feel strange because our big, daily world hides them. But they help us build many real tools, like very small chips, good clocks, and new kinds of light.
